newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RALLYING-ERIKSSON WINS AFTER RIVAL HITS SHEEP.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-ERIKSSON WINS AFTER RIVAL HITS SHEEP.

text.p: Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson won the New Zealand Rally for the first time on Tuesday after his nearest rival Carlos Sainz of Spain hit a sheep on the opening stage of the day.
Eriksson, in a Subaru, finished the third and final leg 13 seconds clear of Sainz of Spain.
Sainz, in a Ford, was second and four times champion Juha Kankunnen of Finland, also in a Ford, third.
"I knew I had to avoid trouble and to finish ahead of Carlos and that was my aim," said Eriksson. "It was bad luck for him to hit that animal, but it gave me a chance and I took it."
His win consolidated the Subaru team's lead in the world manufacturers' championship, but left defending champion Tommi Makinen of Finland top of the drivers' series for Mitsubishi.
Makinen, who crashed out on the opening day, leads with 42 points ahead of Sainz on 34 and Briton Colin McRae, who retired with a camshaft belt failure on his Subaru after leading, third on 32.
After Sainz struck the sheep and lost valuable time, he was fastest on all subsequent stages but failed to overcome the deficit.

"It was on a very fast section in Te Akau," said Sainz. "We were doing around 180 kph, flat out in sixth gear, when we came over a blind crest and saw a sheep standing in the middle of the narrow gravel road.
"It was impossible to avoid and we hit it hard with the front left corner of the car.
"The biggest problem was that a brake pipe was broken in the incident and we had to do the remaining 36 km without brakes to the end of the stage. That is why we lost so much time."
The Spaniard, a double world champion, dropped to fifth on the section and second to third overall.
The incident left him needing Eriksson to make a mistake but the Swede did not. Eriksson was only third on the gravel stage but consolidated his overall lead and stayed there.
He did not win a stage throughout the final day, but always finished close enough to Sainz to retain his advantage as the Spaniard cut the lead from 34 seconds to 13. 050831 GMT aug 97
